sections.html:
Wyandotte County is the smallest county in Kansas, at 156 square miles, and it shares one unified government with its county seat, Kansas City, Kansas. The 2020 population was 169,245. Four cities sit inside the county line: Kansas City, Bonner Springs, Edwardsville and Lake Quivira, which also reaches into Johnson County.

Four school districts cover the county: Turner USD 202, Piper USD 203, Bonner Springs-Edwardsville USD 204 and Kansas City USD 500. Each carries its own value and levy, so the district on your parcel changes the bill.

Because the county is small, one appraiser and one treasurer cover every address, from the river neighborhoods to the interstate retail area.

sections.h2: Who does what: the county offices
sections.html:
The Appraiser values property and the Treasury bills and collects. The Appraiser's page says the office does not set or collect taxes. Taxing districts do that through their budgets, which become the levy.

The Appraiser's Office is open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Pay online through the myWyco site or app, in person (cash, check, money order, or Visa, MasterCard and Discover), by mail with a check or money order, or in the drop box. Payments by phone are not accepted.

The first half is due December 20 and the second half is due May 10. Taxes become a lien on the real estate on November 1. About then each parcel is mailed a tax bill and an information sheet comparing this year's values, rates and taxes with the year before. Parcels with a mortgage escrow get only the information sheet. Not getting a bill does not excuse late payment.

  • If the total tax is at least $10, you can pay in halves without interest.
  • A second-half bill goes out around April 1 to people who paid the first half.
  • Partial payments are accepted, but the unpaid part of the first half keeps accruing interest.
  • Parcels still unpaid on July 25 get a $16 advertising fee and are advertised in August.
  • On the first Tuesday in September, unpaid properties are "sold" to the county, which turns the taxes from current to delinquent.

Call the Treasury for the current interest rate before you compute a payoff.

sections.h2: How a Wyandotte County tax bill is calculated
sections.html:
The appraiser sets value, then each taxing government sets a budget and a mill rate. Residential property is assessed at 11.5% of appraised value, and one mill is $1 of tax per $1,000 of assessed value.

Houses get a break on the school levy. The first $20,000 of a home's appraised value is not subject to the school general levy, so a $100,000 home has two assessed values: $11,500 for most levies and $9,200 for the school general levy. The state sets three levies on its own: 1 mill for educational buildings, one-half mill for correctional buildings, and 40 mills for schools.

Property inside USD 500 also supports the Kansas City, Kansas Public Library, while the rest of the county outside USD 500 and Bonner Springs pays a separate library levy. For current rates, read your own statement or ask the Treasury.

sections.h2: How to appeal your Wyandotte County valuation
sections.html:
File an informal appeal by the date printed on your valuation notice. Notices are mailed in late February with a deadline about a month later. The Appraiser notes that most owners should expect an increase because of limited housing supply, stronger demand and revitalization in parts of the county.

The office lists two reasons for an appeal: the appraised value is higher than the property could reasonably sell for, or the property classification is wrong.

Appeals can go in online, by hand or by mail to the Annex. Meetings can be by phone, on submitted evidence only, virtual or in person. Useful evidence includes a recent fee appraisal, photos of interior or structural problems, and recent sales of comparable properties.

One warning matters a lot: if you start an informal appeal and then abandon it, you cannot pay under protest or appeal again for the same property and tax year. If you miss the deadline, the second chance is a Payment Under Protest, filed in writing with the Treasurer by December 20, or by January 31 if an escrow agent pays at least half. It cannot be used if you already appealed that year, and a first-half protest rules out a second protest for the second half.

Kansas also gives a route to the Board of Tax Appeals within 30 days of the informal decision. The state calendar puts the informal meeting window at May 13 and the final determination at May 20.

sections.h2: When Wyandotte County sells houses for unpaid tax
sections.html:
The Unified Government holds two public auctions a year for tax-sale eligible property. Eligibility depends on the type of property:

  • Homestead properties: delinquent taxes for at least three years
  • Commercial properties: at least two years
  • Vacant and abandoned properties: at least one year

The delinquency count starts on the first Tuesday in September of the year after the levy year. Being eligible does not mean a parcel will be included, since only a limited number go into each sale. Delinquent payments are applied to the most recent delinquent year first, under Charter Resolution CR-01-12.

If you own a vacant or abandoned lot or house, that one-year clock is much shorter than the homestead clock, so check the list sooner rather than later.

sections.h2: Selling a Wyandotte County house with taxes due
sections.html:
Back taxes are a lien, and a title company can pay them from the sale proceeds at closing. Before you list or accept an offer, collect these items:

  1. The parcel number and a current balance from the myWyco site or the Treasury.
  2. Whether the parcel is on the tax sale list, and the date of the next auction.
  3. Any pending appeal, since abandoning one closes off a later protest.
  4. A payoff figure that runs to the closing date, because interest and the August advertising fee change the total.

Cash Home Buyers reviews Wyandotte County houses as they stand, including those with unpaid tax. You decide whether the written offer works against your payoff.

The title company checks the record for liens and unpaid taxes, prepares the deed and totals what comes out of your proceeds. You sign the deed at closing, and the current year's tax is divided between you and the buyer. Bring photo ID and every key, and if a mortgage is open, ask the lender for a payoff figure ahead of time.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill in Wyandotte County?
faqs.a: The Unified Government Treasury sends it. The county Appraiser's Office values the property but does not set or collect the tax.

faqs.q: When is the first half of Wyandotte County property tax due?
faqs.a: December 20. The second half is due May 10, and halves are allowed without interest when the total tax is at least $10.

faqs.q: What is the Wyandotte County appeal deadline?
faqs.a: It is the date printed on your valuation notice. Notices are mailed in late February, and the deadline falls about a month later.

faqs.q: How long before Wyandotte County can sell a house at a tax sale?
faqs.a: For homestead property, delinquent taxes must be at least three years old. Commercial property needs two years and vacant or abandoned property needs one.

faqs.q: Do Wyandotte County homeowners get a school tax break?
faqs.a: Yes. The first $20,000 of a residence's appraised value is not subject to the school general levy, so a house carries two assessed values.
